Subject: Tenant onboarding: next steps and environment checklist

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the quick response during the demo — our infra team is ready to start the private deployment onboarding. Before we lock times, can you send the minimal network/account prerequisites and an initial checklist we can run against our environment?

High level asks from our side:
- IP allowlist requirements and whether you support dynamic ranges (we use a mix of static and auto-assigned egress IPs)
- VPN vs. PrivateLink/Peering options and recommended ports (we have strict egress policies)
- KMS/HSM integration notes (we use AWS KMS)
- Any procurement info your side needs (SOW, PO templates)

If you already have a single-page intake checklist for the networking team that would be ideal — otherwise a short spreadsheet is fine.

Thanks,
Julia Park

Subject: Re: Tenant onboarding: next steps and environment checklist

Hi Julia —

Appreciate the list. I attached our lightweight onboarding checklist and a starter VPC template to make the intake as painless as possible. At a glance:

Key network prerequisites (summary):
- Public egress: provide 2 static egress IPs for outbound allowlisting OR request our NAT IP range authorization for dynamic egress.
- BGP/peering: we support cloud VPC peering (AWS) and routable VPN; if you prefer peering, please provide route table CIDRs and a contact for the peering ticket.
- Ports: 443 outbound required, 5222 for internal agent (optional), and ICMP for health checks unless you prefer TCP-only.
- Service accounts: one service account for install + one service account for long-term monitoring with described IAM roles (attached template).
- KMS: we support AWS KMS key policies — provide key ARN and admin contact; we will need decrypt/encrypt permission for the Redwood service principal during onboarding.

I also listed a minimal evidence matrix we need for SOC/controls (log retention, audit log access, and encryption at rest).

Attachments included: statera_onboarding_checklist_v1.pdf (PDF, 210 KB), redwood_vpc_template.yaml (YAML, 4 KB), network_inventory.xlsx (XLSX, 48 KB).

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick kick-off call (30 min) to align on peering vs VPN and confirm egress approach — is Friday 9/11 10:00am PT OK?
2) Your infra team completes the checklist and returns network_inventory.xlsx.
3) We schedule a hands-on workshop for the peering/VPN setup and KMS key exchange.

Looping in Ben (private deployments lead) and Naomi (security/compliance) to confirm technical intake and evidence items.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Manager, Customer Onboarding — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Tenant onboarding: next steps and environment checklist

Thanks — quick technical clarifications from our side before the call:

1) Egress IPs: if Statera can provide static NAT IPs for the tenant, we'll prefer allowlisting those. If not, we can work with a short-lived authorization token and record the observed egress ranges during testing.

2) Peering vs VPN: Peering (AWS VPC peering) is preferred for consistent performance; we need your route table entries and the peering owner account id. Managed VPN is fine as a fallback (we'll need to exchange pre-shared keys and coordinate uptime windows).

3) KMS access: Provide the key ARN and a cross-account grant to 'redwood-inference-service' principal. Naomi — can you confirm the exact minimum IAM permissions we should request in the grant?

4) Ports/health checks: We'll default to TCP 443 for control plane, 9443 for runtime telemetry, and ICMP only for initial smoke tests. Please flag if policy blocks ICMP.

I'll prepare a short network diagram for the call.

-ben
Ben Carter
Lead, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference

Julia — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming our agreed plan from the kickoff:

- Kickoff call scheduled: Fri 9/11, 10:00am PT (30 min) — meeting invite sent separately.
- Action items for Statera (owner in parens):
  1) Complete network_inventory.xlsx and return by Tue 9/15 (Julia / ops-team).
  2) Provide either two static NAT egress IPs OR confirm dynamic egress authorization method (ops-team).
  3) Share KMS key ARN and a point of contact for key grants (security@staterahealth.com).
  4) If choosing peering: provide AWS account id and target route table CIDRs; if VPN: provide gateway IP and preferred maintenance windows.

- Action items for Redwood:
  1) Ben will draft the minimal IAM policy for KMS and a peering checklist by Mon 9/14.
  2) Naomi will enumerate the evidence items we need for encrypted-at-rest and audit logs (separate doc).
  3) I'll coordinate the workshop and open a HubSpot onboarding record (DEAL-3281).

Attachments referenced in this thread are included again for easy reference: statera_onboarding_checklist_v1.pdf, network_inventory.xlsx, redwood_vpc_template.yaml.

If anything changes before the call, reply-all so we keep a single timeline. Looking forward to the workshop.

Best regards,
